workstreams.title: Who said Theranos used the wrong technology?
workstreams.status: Speaker and full exchange not authenticated
workstreams.summary: Investigate the remembered statement without turning a plausible technical explanation into an attributed quotation.

findings.label: Sample preparation is not continuous manual intervention
findings.text: The miniLab supporting workflow describes operator aliquoting and cartridge loading, then says no further operator intervention is required after protocol initiation. That is positive evidence of protocol automation in the reported experiments. It is not proof of a fully autonomous patient-to-result service, broad-menu integration or first-attempt reliability. Criticism should identify the actual missing capability rather than imply nothing was automated.

findings.label: The paper itself says integration was incomplete
findings.text: Printed p65 states that the then-current platform could not contain all modules in one chassis; full functionality in one device was future work. It also acknowledges one cartridge at a time and data for only one assay/panel per cartridge. This narrows the demonstrated platform claim without denying the selected assay results. It does not independently identify the film's device or establish the engineer's intended criticism.

findings.label: Accuracy after retesting is not first-attempt reliability
findings.text: Supporting methods disclose invalid runs, retests and exclusions. HSV-2 comparison had 21 runs meeting exclusion criteria, all repeated; lipid comparison had 13, with seven repeated and six runs from four subjects excluded; lymphocyte comparison had seven, with two retested and five subjects excluded. These disclosures are not proof of misconduct. Do not divide by final specimen counts to invent an attempt-failure rate; retained-result accuracy, first-attempt yield, turnaround and cost are separate questions.

findings.label: The assay demonstrations were not a universal fingerstick workflow
findings.text: Supporting Table 1 specifies whole blood, serum or plasma according to the assay, with loaded volumes of 30 or 160 microlitres and run times of 45–140 minutes. Zika sensitivity used spiked venous blood; other comparisons used venous serum/plasma or cell samples, some adjusted to abnormal concentrations. These are disclosed experiments, not independent end-to-end fingerstick validation. Loaded volume, protocol consumption and original collection volume must not be conflated.

findings.label: Which Theranos machine actually tested patients?
findings.text: The amended appellate opinion states that Edison was the only Theranos-developed device used for patient testing; miniLab and other devices remained in development. It distinguishes 300 developed small-sample assays from twelve ever run on Edison. This is the court's selected account of trial evidence, not an independently reconstructed assay inventory. A later prototype demonstration cannot establish earlier deployed capability.

findings.label: Platform meant shared engineering, not a universal sensor
findings.text: The 2018 company-authored engineering paper describes miniLab hardware, assay-configurable cartridges and a connected server called the virtual analyzer. It reports selected illustrative genetic, antibody, lipid and cell measurements using different modules. All authors were current/former Theranos employees with possible equity interests. This supports a real engineering programme, not independent replication, universal clinical validation or proof of 2013–2014 readiness.

findings.label: A tiny sample must still be representative
findings.text: Bond and Richards-Kortum found greater drop-to-drop variability in several cellular measurements from fingerprick blood than in venous controls, with improved consistency at larger sampled volumes in their experiment. This was not a Theranos-machine evaluation and does not show all fingerstick tests fail. Collection and preparation require validation alongside the analyser; a better sensor does not by itself establish representative sampling.

findings.label: Different technology is not inherited proof of success
findings.text: Haemanthus's application describes a Raman system using pump and Stokes beams; a distinct 2026 USPTO grant covers counterpropagating beams and names LaChapelle and Cannon. These establish an optical architecture and specific patent rights, not broad clinical accuracy or the film engineer's identity. Whether this was the speaker's intended contrast remains unverified.

findings.label: A documented role is not speaker identification
findings.text: Forbes identifies Joseph LaChapelle as Haemanthus's former CTO and quotes his email saying he resigned on 16 March 2026. The article also reports a conflicting second-hand account attributed to Evans. This strengthens the employment-role lead, but does not identify the on-screen engineer or authenticate the remembered criticism. Do not settle the departure dispute from these accounts alone.

findings.label: What technological contrast can be established?
findings.text: The SEC complaint describes the earlier Theranos analyser as limited to immunochemistry and the proposed miniLab as an attempt to integrate more test methods; it alleges the broader device was not clinically ready at launch. Haemanthus's published application concerns Raman spectroscopy instead. Different detection principles do not by themselves establish better clinical performance. These records explain a contrast, not the unidentified speaker's verified argument.

findings.label: Did any Theranos technology work?
findings.text: FDA K143236 cleared a specific HSV-1 IgG assay in July 2015 for specified uses and specimens, including fingerstick whole blood. The 7 July letter corrects a 2 July letter. This is a genuine, limited regulatory achievement—not clearance of a universal platform or validation of every prior claim. The blanket statement that nothing worked is too broad.

findings.label: Independent evidence about the delivered service
findings.text: A 2016 JCI study compared 22 measurements in 60 healthy adults across Theranos, Quest and LabCorp. It found significant interservice differences and more out-of-range flags at Theranos. This is independent published evidence of service-level concerns, not proof every Theranos result was wrong, a device teardown or validation of every assay and patient population.

findings.label: What the film sources establish
findings.text: The distributor describes a film following Holmes and later events over three years. KPBS reports Evans's later venture, Haemanthus. Neither inspected passage identifies the engineer or authenticates the remembered exchange. Unauthorised CAM/subtitle search results were not used as verified film evidence.

findings.label: A separate technical lead—not speaker identification
findings.text: A published Haemanthus application, US20250277701A1, names Joseph G. LaChapelle and Roger S. Cannon and concerns Raman spectroscopy. A patent record does not identify an on-screen speaker, establish their employment at a particular date or prove a working diagnostic product. This application must not be called a granted patent.

findings.label: What would make the criticism testable?
findings.text: Separate sample preparation, assay chemistry, optical detection, instrument integration and business economics. Raman spectroscopy examines light scattered by molecular vibrations; translating spectra into a reliable clinical result still needs calibration, interference testing and independent clinical validation. An alternative detection method does not by itself solve all the sample or validation problems. This is a general technical explanation, not the unidentified speaker's verified argument.

gaps: A lawful checked film passage, speaker caption or authenticated credits, edition and timestamp.
The complete question and answer: which analyte, earlier device, alternative method and evidence were being compared?
Dated source evidence linking any proposed speaker to this particular passage. No identity has been assigned from a patent name or visual resemblance.

workstreams.title: An investor case study: Lisa Peterson's evidence
workstreams.status: Investor financials, committee memo and closing documents identified in selected testimony; full transaction file still incomplete
workstreams.summary: Peterson's evidence links an October 2014 meeting, financials and her own investment-committee memo. It distinguishes expectations of existing proprietary capability from future forecasts, with cross-examination and contrary pharmaceutical evidence alongside it.

findings.label: Prepared for Pfizer is not prepared by Pfizer
findings.text: Exhibit 0143 PDF p3 / report p1 bears the Theranos logo and identifies the Angiogenesis Study Report as prepared for Dr Aidan Power at Pfizer. That is not by itself a Pfizer-authored endorsement. Separately, the government's 2023 answering brief PDF p15 reproduces two covers: one says prepared for a named Pfizer doctor; the other carries a Pfizer logo and omits that prepared-for wording. Those are a party's selected record images, not two complete standalone reports or proof of which exact scan reached every investor.

findings.label: What technology was the early study actually about?
findings.text: Exhibit 0143 PDF pp5–7 / report pp3–5 describes monitoring response to anti-angiogenesis therapies. It reports 32 enrolled patients and three simultaneous fingerstick assays: VEGF, soluble VEGF receptor R2 and placental growth factor. Its system combines a reader, single-use chemistry/control cartridge and cellular connection to protocols, computation and a web portal. This explains a concrete early platform concept: repeated remote measurement of a small marker panel. These are Theranos's reported design and study claims, not independent verification of every result, identification of the film's device or validation of a later universal diagnostic menu.

findings.label: The report itself discloses changing assay ranges
findings.text: Exhibit 0143 PDF p8 / report p6 says cartridge specifications changed as patient samples became available. It reports early VEGF calibration stopping at 3,000 pg/mL before extension to 10,000 pg/mL, and early placental-growth-factor sensitivity of 50 pg/mL producing many out-of-range-low results. Later lots are described as reaching below 20 pg/mL. These are company-reported limitations and improvements, not independently reproduced performance. Our technical interpretation: a claim that the platform works needs a dated cartridge lot, assay range and intended specimen/use; an instrument name or headline correlation does not establish the whole menu's clinical reliability.

findings.label: What did the investor think the report represented?
findings.text: Printed pp4681–4683 (PDF pp101–103) connect the reports to Peterson's diligence binder. She says she believed the Pfizer-logo report was prepared by Pfizer, attributed that impression to the logo, did not recall seeing prepared-for wording and was not told it was Theranos's work unapproved by Pfizer. Asked whether Theranos's own conclusions would carry the same relevance, she says not nearly as much. This narrows the reliance question: perceived independent authorship mattered, not just the existence of an experimental study. It remains her testimony, not our inspection of the complete investor binder.

findings.label: Holmes's explanation belongs beside the accusation
findings.text: On printed pp7478–7482 (PDF pp35–39), Holmes admits adding the logos just before sending reports to Walgreens. She says she intended to convey partnership, denied intending to imply pharmaceutical authorship and expressed regret about the presentation. She identifies Defence Exhibit 15048 as a January 2014 email from Christian Holmes to Pfizer recipients, with her copied, attaching what she says was the same Pfizer-logo version sent to Walgreens. This is her account and the defence's non-concealment argument. Sending a report to Pfizer is not proof Pfizer approved its wording, logo or conclusions; we have not inspected the standalone email, attachments or replies.

findings.label: What the Pfizer witness actually denied
findings.text: On printed pp4396–4400 (PDF pp79–83), Shane Weber is shown Walgreens email Exhibit 291 describing reports as independent due diligence, and a comparison with Exhibit 143. He says he did not approve the logo and knew of no Pfizer approval, while explaining that legal/trademark staff—not he—would authorise external logo use. He rejects the propositions that Pfizer endorsed or comprehensively validated Theranos technology in 2010 or after. His lack of knowledge of permission is not an exhaustive audit of Pfizer records, and rejection of endorsement does not prove no experimental work occurred. The dispute concerns authorship, endorsement and validation scope, not whether a document existed.

findings.label: How much was this particular investment?
findings.text: On printed pp4697–4698 (PDF pp117–118), Peterson identifies Dynasty Financial II LLC as the legal investing entity on RDV's behalf. Questioned about admitted Exhibit 4845, she confirms $99,999,984 as the investment amount and 31 October 2014 as its approximate date. This supports describing this case as an approximately $100m investment; it is not a claim about every DeVos family member's participation. We have inspected the transcript, not the standalone transaction document or bank statement. The amount does not establish what Theranos spent the proceeds on.

findings.label: Exhibit 2166: the investor's memo, not a Theranos pitch deck
findings.text: On printed pp4691–4693 (PDF pp111–113), Peterson identifies Government Exhibit 2166 as the RDV approval document she prepared after the 14 October 2014 meeting for the investment committee. It was admitted without objection. She confirms the document's 31 October 2014 closing date as approximate. This is direct evidence about the investor's written synthesis, not inspection of the complete standalone memo or proof of every committee discussion. Do not attribute its authorship to Holmes or confuse it with investor financials Exhibit 1853 or internal projections Exhibit 15031.

findings.label: What mattered: proprietary equipment and portability
findings.text: Printed pp4693–4697 (PDF pp113–117) record Peterson saying that manufacture of the analyser equipment was relevant to underwriting. A memo passage describes a small analyser station that could be placed in an operating room, military evacuation helicopter, ship or refugee camp; she attributes that information to Holmes and Balwani and calls portability critical to her understanding. This is a claimed capability with potential deployment locations, not evidence of actual military use. She also says she was never told before investing that third-party machines did some or most testing, or that the TSPU ran no more than twelve assays. Those are her sworn recollections, not recordings of the meeting or proof that every investor heard the same claims.

findings.label: 900 locations in 2015 was a plan, not 900 operating sites
findings.text: Printed pp4694–4695 (PDF pp114–115) quote the memo's planned 900 Walgreens wellness centres in five metropolitan markets the following year. Peterson attributes it to the Palo Alto conversation and denies being told locations were being scaled back. Treat the number as a forecast. Separately, the amended appellate opinion pp14–15 recounts Walgreens testimony that the partnership was contracting while expansion was being promoted. A future rollout target and the actual state of a partnership are different propositions: failure to achieve the former alone does not establish that the latter was honestly described.

findings.label: Pharmaceutical credibility was influential—but disputed
findings.text: Printed pp4693–4694 (PDF pp113–114) record a memo assertion of comprehensive validation by ten pharmaceutical companies. The spoken date is corrected from 2015 to 2005; this remains an attributed assertion, not an established validation history. Peterson says validation, including Pfizer, mattered to underwriting. The court overruled a Rule 602 objection: that kept the answers in evidence, it did not certify scientific performance. The amended appellate opinion p15 recounts Holmes admitting she added pharmaceutical logos to reports, and company representatives denying independent validation or permission to use their logos. A report carrying a familiar logo is not automatically an independently authored validation study.

findings.label: The defence counterpoint: what could she actually recall?
findings.text: On printed pp4711–4712 (PDF pp131–132), Peterson could not recall the Pfizer study's kind, location, drug or particular tests. She nevertheless described reading the reports at the time and taking them as support for analyser accuracy; she rejected the suggestion that she remembered only the logo. This limits how precisely her later testimony can reconstruct scientific diligence. It neither establishes that no diligence occurred nor supplies missing independent validation. Her stated investment impression and the underlying scientific evidence must be checked separately.

findings.label: Who approved, signed and could release the funds?
findings.text: Printed pp4696 and 4719–4721 (PDF pp116 and 139–141) distinguish the committee document from closing authority. Peterson identifies Tubergen and Damstra signatures on the memo. On cross-examination, Defence Exhibit 2170 is admitted as a closing email; she confirms signed documentation was sent by Tubergen to Balwani on 31 October 2014 and identifies Robert Schierbeek as the Dynasty Financial signatory, RDV COO and person authorised to disburse the funds. This narrows the decision-process gap but is not a bank receipt, proof of the actual transfer date or the full committee minutes. Peterson was not the only participant in the investment process.

findings.label: A demonstration needs an instrument-to-result trail
findings.text: The amended appellate opinion recounts employee testimony that some VIP demonstrations ran a null protocol on the displayed Theranos device while samples were tested elsewhere on third-party equipment. This is the court's account of trial evidence, not our reconstruction of every visit. A visitor seeing a machine and receiving a result therefore does not, without a linked run record, establish that the displayed machine produced that result. This concerns represented present capability, not merely a future forecast.

findings.label: The decisive test is dated capability, not whether innovation was possible
findings.text: Read each representation in its own tense: what already operated, what was under development, and what financial outcome was forecast. Grossman's 2013 testimony and Peterson's 2014 testimony concern different encounters. The 2015 limited assay clearance and later miniLab paper cannot retrospectively establish the earlier broad capability. This is our comparison of the cited records, not a finding that all investors received the same pitch or that every unfulfilled ambition was fraudulent.

findings.label: Which investor-facing document was identified?
findings.text: Peterson identified Exhibit 1853 as annotated financials received in a diligence binder and discussed with Holmes and Balwani in October 2014. The court-hosted Balwani Exhibit 4859, RDV012671, has been visually inspected: $140m/$990m projected 2014/2015 revenue, $230m projected 2015 net income and a 900-locations annotation. Selected Holmes cross-examination also identifies Exhibit 1853, that annotation and the $990m forecast. This is a strong feature match, not an authenticated exhibit-number/Bates cross-reference; exact scan identity remains unresolved.

findings.label: December 2013: an operating business, not just future research
findings.text: Grossman testified that Holmes and Balwani described technology better than conventional laboratory equipment, already used on human samples and generating reimbursement, with an intended Walgreens expansion. He also testified that third-party machine use had not been disclosed to him; questions about margin assumptions show its commercial relevance. This is sworn recollection, not a meeting recording or evidence that every investor heard identical statements. A missed forecast alone does not establish deception.

findings.label: What did the capability claims actually say?
findings.text: SEC complaint paragraphs 53–60 allege present capability claims covering over 1,000 CPT codes, a solution for another 300, tests on one analyser and one consumable, and manufacture of all analysers despite third-party use. Billing codes are not a count of distinct validated assays. These remain civil allegations; the criminal investor-fraud verdict is a separate legal record. Assess each investor's actual materials, qualifications and reliance, not an undifferentiated pitch.

findings.label: Future forecast versus present starting point
findings.text: Peterson acknowledged the statement was projected. She explained that receiving a December forecast in October suggested the company was at or close to the projection. That interpretation is witness evidence, not a rule that forecasts are guarantees. Existing capability and business-condition claims must be tested separately; a missed forecast alone is not proof of fraud. Keep the SEC's allegations distinct from the DOJ-reported criminal investor-fraud verdict.

findings.label: Who actually invested?
findings.text: On printed p4717 (PDF p137), cross-examination identifies Dynasty Financial II LLC as the investing entity. Peterson said she did not know all its beneficial owners. RDV's investment review, the legal investing entity and a shorthand reference to the DeVos family are not interchangeable. The passage does not establish every owner's allocation or reconcile all payments.

findings.label: What the appellate opinion records
findings.text: The amended opinion places Peterson among 2014 C-2 investors and recounts her testimony that financial documents received from Holmes and Balwani projected $230 million profit by the end of 2015. This is the court's account of trial evidence, not her complete transcript or investment file.

findings.label: A matching number is not proof of delivery
findings.text: Exhibit 15031 includes a July 2014 internal email and projections containing $230 million 2015 net income. This numerical match does not establish that this exact version was delivered to Peterson, when she received it, its accompanying qualifications or the decisions it influenced.

findings.label: What this already clarifies
findings.text: A financial forecast is explicitly about a future period. A claim that a proprietary instrument already performs a test is about present capability. An investment pitch can contain both, and uncertainty in the forecast does not automatically qualify the separate technical representation. Establish actual delivery and reliance before explaining why this investor invested.

gaps: Complete direct/cross-examination and standalone Exhibits 1853, 2166 and Defence 2170; exact scan identity and comparison with internal Exhibit 15031.

Complete investor binder, later branded report versions, raw study data and independent performance review. Selected pages of court-hosted Exhibit 0143 have now been inspected; that does not close the full study/version gap.
Standalone Defence Exhibit 15048, Pfizer replies and full legal/trademark approval records; a reported transmission is not endorsement.
Payment reconciliation, complete beneficial ownership, committee minutes and all decision-makers' roles. Selected testimony does not establish every discussion, owner or motive.
A checked film passage: the film is not a transaction file, and absence from our notes is not proof of omission from the film.

workstreams.title: What did Theranos patent—and what did it prove?
workstreams.status: Granted-claim reading; product implementation and legal title not verified
workstreams.summary: A first claim-by-claim map of US8283155B2 distinguishes protected architecture from evidence of clinical performance.

findings.label: A real cartridge platform is not a universal blood-testing platform
findings.text: FDA K160457 concerns FilmArray BCID with FilmArray Torch: a defined molecular panel on positive blood cultures already identified by monitoring and Gram stain. Its pouch supports nucleic-acid purification and nested multiplex PCR with melt analysis. Preparation/loading precedes the instrument-controlled protocol. This is a narrow-use comparator, not direct-fingerstick universal testing, validation of Theranos or proof of patent infringement.

findings.label: The patents were asserted after closure—but value was not adjudicated
findings.text: Labrador's March 2020 complaint asserted US8283155B2 and US10533994B2 against BioFire/bioMerieux, alleging ownership by assignment. A subsequent notice dismissed the case without prejudice. These records establish an assertion and dismissal, not proven infringement, a completed title-chain audit, royalties, damages, clinical utility or a sale valuation. The plaintiff's explanations for dismissal remain its account.

findings.label: A separate granted optical design—not a diagnostic certificate
findings.text: The USPTO's 10 November 2026 record identifies US12791485B2, Raman spectroscopy with counterpropagating pump and Stokes beams, assigned to Haemanthus and naming Joseph G. LaChapelle and Roger S. Cannon. This is distinct from application US20250277701A1. It establishes a particular granted design, not a clinically validated replacement for Theranos, comprehensive legal title, freedom to operate or identification of the film engineer.

findings.label: Recorded transactions narrow the ownership question
findings.text: The Google Patents event list for US8283155B2 records a December 2017 assignment to Theranos IP Company and a separate Fortress security interest, a 2020 name change to Labrador Diagnostics, and July 2023 assignments through Golden Diagnostics Top Corp. to Golden Diagnostics Corp. These are database-recorded events, not inspection of the underlying instruments or a current legal-title opinion. A security interest must not be called an outright ownership transfer.

findings.label: The granted claim's centre
findings.text: Claim 1 concerns a two-way communication system: a reader, an external protocol source and an identified test device with a sample collector and assay reactants. Dependent claim 9 adds collection below about 500 microlitres. That limit is not itself a claim that all tests run from one drop.

findings.label: Ownership and dates need their own evidence
findings.text: The record lists Theranos as original assignee and 9 October 2012 as the grant publication date. Later database ownership labels do not establish legal title at every investment date. Check the assignment instruments and prosecution history before making an ownership, validity or freedom-to-operate conclusion.

findings.label: Architecture is not validation
findings.text: A claim can define an invention without proving that a commercial device implemented it reliably, met a clinical acceptance criterion, delivered a broad menu or justified an investor representation. Product mapping below is deliberately unverified rather than inferred from a similar diagram.

gaps: A dated product configuration, schematics, software/protocol records and assay validation for each proposed mapping.
Assignment instruments and patent prosecution history, not merely a current database label.
A specialist's reading of claim scope, dependencies and relevant alternatives. This is not legal advice or an infringement opinion.

workstreams.title: A film companion you can verify scene by scene
workstreams.status: Two-part production account documented; individual scene times still unchecked
workstreams.summary: The filmmakers describe Holmes/Evans footage followed by later work with Seyfried. This account clarifies the structure but is not a checked scene-by-scene edition audit.

findings.label: The reconstruction has a different evidence status
findings.text: Oppenheim says later reenactments used scripts based on the filmmakers' memory notes, while describing the filmed encounters as unscripted reactions. That is an attributed production claim, not our audit of rushes or scripts. A memory-based performance is not a contemporaneous recording of the reconstructed exchange.

findings.label: How to test the film's present-versus-future argument
findings.text: For each relevant scene, record the exact statement, speaker, edition and surrounding question. Compare it with the dated investor record, not a later prototype. Our investor chronology separates 2013 operating claims, 2014 forecasts, 2015 limited clearance and 2018 engineering results. Without a checked passage we cannot conclude that the film contradicts, explains or omits a particular record; absence from our notes is not proof of absence from the film.

findings.label: Nodding is observable; its cause is not established
findings.text: A checked recording could establish when a nod occurs and which question, pause or edit surrounds it. It cannot by itself establish lying, agreement, a medical condition or a psychological motive. Compare complete exchanges, camera continuity and possible listening behaviour before interpreting a gesture. No frequency count or behavioural diagnosis has been made here.

findings.label: A participant disputes what the kitchen-table device establishes
findings.text: In a STAT opinion, Tyler Shultz describes the kitchen-table unit as a later unfinished product rather than the Edison he used, and describes external preparation for Edison testing. This is a participant's counter-account, not our independent identification of the filmed unit. It makes device/version/date mapping a priority. His speculation about motives, filmmaker knowledge or mental state is not adopted.

findings.label: Is the first half Holmes or an actress?
findings.text: In the 11 November 2026 participant interview, Fielder describes filming at the beach house with Holmes and Evans, then approaching Seyfried roughly two years later and showing her what became the first half. Seyfried describes around 90 minutes of footage. Fielder says her recreations concerned initial conversations that happened off-camera. This supports genuine Holmes footage followed by a film also using performance—not a secretly actor-played entire first half. It remains the participants' edited account, not independent verification of each shot or a timestamp boundary.

findings.label: Runtime does not identify a scene
findings.text: IDFA lists 174 minutes. That programme runtime does not establish the edition, distributor cards, start convention or location of any remembered passage in the Liverpool screening. Record those details before aligning different viewers' notes.

findings.label: Separate recording and performance at passage level
findings.text: The participant interview supports a performance element. A usable scene record must identify the visible performer, voice, script source, archive inserts and reconstruction notices separately. It must not assume a perfectly clean division into two halves.

findings.label: What has actually been done
findings.text: The records below are explicit verification tasks with empty time fields. No lawful viewing copy or authenticated transcript has been inspected for this workstream, and no timestamp is represented as checked. A contributor can supply a short necessary description and locator without uploading the film.

gaps: A lawfully accessible film edition or authenticated transcript/continuity script.
Checked start/end times, surrounding dialogue and any performance disclosure for each passage.
Independent checking before a proposed timestamp becomes an editorial finding.

workstreams.title: Theranos financial records: forecasts are not spending
workstreams.status: Historical accounts, closure letter and later creditor settlement located; no complete cash ledger
workstreams.summary: Trial evidence and a court-hosted valuation extend the financial record. Forecasts, historical company accounts, reported balances and cash payments remain separate.

findings.label: Later evidence that the creditor assignment occurred
findings.text: The 2023 ABC agreement's recital records a General Assignment executed on 12 September 2018. That advances the evidence beyond the closure letter's proposal. It is later contractual evidence, not inspection of the original assignment instrument or proof of the IP subsidiary's title chain. Those distinct instruments remain needed.

findings.label: A $45m allowed claim is not a $45m recovery
findings.text: ABC agreement sections 1–2 allow separate $45m unsecured Walgreens and class claims. The class distribution is specified as $1,331,094.88, due within ten days after the required approval; Walgreens's claim participates pro rata. The February 2024 order approves implementation, with ABC approval concerning class claims. These are claim and payment terms, not a receipt, total estate valuation or original spending ledger.

findings.label: Walgreens's $44m is separate from Theranos's remaining estate
findings.text: Definitions 36–37 in the Walgreens agreement require Walgreens to fund $44m in cash into the settlement fund. This is a separate payer and obligation from the ABC estate's class distribution. Neither belongs in a total of historical Theranos research or operating expenditure. Settlement funding, allowed claims, gross funds and net class receipts are different figures; completed payment and final deductions need their own evidence.

findings.label: September 2018: what the company said was left
findings.text: Taylor's 4 September 2018 letter, filed as Exhibit D, reports default under the Fortress credit facility, at least $60m owed to unsecured creditors and roughly $5m remaining cash net of fees/expenses. It anticipates no shareholder distribution. This is a contemporaneous company account, not audited balances, final creditor recoveries or a reconstruction of 2015–2018 spending. Funding minus this balance must not be called money spent.

findings.label: A proposed wind-down is not proof of completed IP transfer
findings.text: The same letter describes a possible Fortress settlement involving the IP subsidiary, an assignment for the benefit of creditors and dissolution. Its final page says board/shareholder consents will be sought. Contacts with over 80 potential sale counterparties and 17 NDAs reportedly produced no sale. The letter alone does not prove completed settlement, title transfer, final sale value or distributions; executed instruments and final accounts remain needed.

findings.label: 2014 and a short 2015 period: historical accounts located
findings.text: Exhibit 5209 reproduces an Aranca historical income statement in $'000. Dec-14 FY-A shows $150,000 revenue, $100.031m operating costs, $7.095m depreciation and a $106.666m loss. Mar-15 / 2 Mth-A shows $14,000 revenue, $22.961m operating costs, $5.691m depreciation and a $28.648m loss. Preserve the unusual period labels: do not call this a complete quarter or annualise it. These are actual-labelled company figures reproduced in a valuation, not audited cash expenditure.

findings.label: Cash balances are not a spending reconciliation
findings.text: The next Aranca page reports cash/equivalents of $463.310m at Dec-14 and $557.081m at Mar-15. Financing and other cash movements can affect balances; the difference is not money spent. Depreciation, operating costs, loss, financing and closing cash are different accounting measures. Do not add depreciation or R&D twice, or silently reconcile earlier testimony and differing revenue definitions.

findings.label: Keep forecasts, revenue and IRS total income distinct
findings.text: The SEC complaint's $108m figure is an allegedly supplied investor financial, not actual revenue; it describes actual 2014 recorded revenue as little over $100,000. The valuation's $150,000 historical figure needs accounting/version reconciliation, not silent replacement. The appellate opinion recounts $1,944,948 total income reported to the IRS in 2015: that is not a full-year customer-revenue or spending ledger, and the underlying tax return has not been inspected here.

findings.label: Actual expense evidence—not another forecast
findings.text: On printed pp780–781 (PDF pp121–122), controller So-Han Spivey discusses consolidated income statements admitted as Defence Exhibit 4176. She gives operating expenses/R&D of $28.2m/$22m for 2011, about $67m/$53m for 2012 and about $92m/$68m for 2013, agreeing significant R&D contributed to operating losses. This is evidence of substantial research expenditure, not proof all funding vanished or went on personal extravagance. It is testimony about accounting expenses, not an independent audit or a complete cash ledger; amounts are rounded as stated.

findings.label: Three different statements in one exhibit
findings.text: Exhibit 15031 contains projected income, proforma cash flow and a company-reported 14 July 2014 balance sheet. The balance sheet uses thousands of dollars; the forecast tables use dollars. A reported balance is not independently audited cash, and neither a deficit nor a forecast expense is a paid-cash ledger.

findings.label: A court-described counterweight
findings.text: The opinion recounts controller testimony of $92 million net loss in 2013 and a November 2013 internal account of up to $2 million weekly spending. Those figures are not a period-wide, independently reconstructed cash ledger; do not multiply a weekly rate into an invented total.

findings.label: Arithmetic discrepancies are questions, not intent findings
findings.text: The reproduced forecasts contain differences between labelled net-income figures and between displayed closing balances and arithmetic. The checks below use the printed values without silently repairing them. Underlying worksheets, definitions and rounding policies are needed before explaining the differences.

gaps: Defence Exhibit 4176 itself and further period-matched statements, cash ledgers, reconciliations and expense detail. Selected 2011–2013 expense testimony is now located.

scene_records.title: Domestic documentary access
scene_records.question: Who is visible and speaking? Is any archive, reconstructed speech or production disclosure present?

scene_records.title: Seyfried performance material
scene_records.question: Where does performance begin and end, and what is the script or speech source?

scene_records.title: Remembered wrong-technology exchange
scene_records.question: Authenticate speaker, full question/answer and the specific device or method being criticised.

scene_records.title: Present capability versus future possibility
scene_records.question: Preserve tense, date, qualifiers and surrounding question. Compare with the investor case and contemporary documents.

expert_briefs.question: Which assay/sample-specific evidence would establish or refute a claimed testing capability?
expert_briefs.deliverable: One sourced correction or validation critique, naming device, analyte, sample and date.
expert_briefs.conflicts: Disclose relevant employment, consulting, litigation or commercial interests; no patient data.

expert_briefs.question: Does the proposed detection approach address the specific failure mode, or merely change the measurement principle?
expert_briefs.deliverable: A diagram or short sourced comparison separating collection, preparation, optics and inference.
expert_briefs.conflicts: Disclose patent, employer and product interests; do not reveal trade secrets.

expert_briefs.question: Is our reading of claims 1 and 9 accurate, and which documents would establish product mapping and relevant ownership?
expert_briefs.deliverable: A source-located claim-chart correction with legal and technical limits.
expert_briefs.conflicts: Disclose representation or financial interests; no client-confidential material.

expert_briefs.question: Which figures are comparable, and what can the forecast differences establish without a ledger?
expert_briefs.deliverable: A checked arithmetic or classification correction tied to exact exhibit pages.
expert_briefs.conflicts: Disclose company, investor or litigation work; no private bank or employee records.

expert_briefs.question: How should recording, performance and reconstructed speech be coded for this edition?
expert_briefs.deliverable: A lawful scene locator and short contextual correction, not an uploaded film copy.
expert_briefs.conflicts: Disclose production, distribution or promotional involvement.
